(a) Interagency Budget Crosscut and Coordination Report.—
        (1) In general.—The Secretary of Homeland Security, the Administrator, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, and the heads of each Federal department or agency carrying out activities under sections 100215 and 100216 shall work together to ensure that flood risk determination data and geospatial data are shared among Federal agencies in 
order to coordinate the efforts of the Nation to reduce its vulnerability to flooding hazards. 
        (2) Report.—Not later than 30 days after the submission of the budget of the United States Government by the President to Congress, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, in coordination with the Federal Emergency Management Agency, the United States Geological Survey, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, the Corps of Engineers, and other Federal agencies, as appropriate, shall submit to the appropriate authorizing and appropriating committees of the Senate and the House of Representatives an interagency budget crosscut and coordination report, certified by the Secretary or head of each such agency, that—
            (A) contains an interagency budget crosscut report that displays relevant sections of the budget proposed for each of the Federal agencies working on flood risk determination data and digital elevation models, including any planned interagency or intra-agency transfers; and 
            (B) describes how the efforts aligned with such sections complement one another.   
    (b) Duties of the Administrator.—In carrying out sections 100215 and 100216, the Administrator shall—
        (1) participate, pursuant to section 216 of the E–Government Act of 2002 (44 U.S.C. 3501 note), in the establishment of such standards and common protocols as are necessary to assure the interoperability of geospatial data for all users of such information; 
        (2) coordinate with, seek assistance and cooperation of, and provide a liaison to the Federal Geographic Data Committee pursuant to the Office of Management and Budget Circular A–16 and Executive Order 12906 (43 U.S.C. 1457 note; relating to the National Spatial Data Infrastructure) for the implementation of and compliance with such standards; 
        (3) integrate with, leverage, and coordinate funding of, to the maximum extent practicable, the current flood mapping activities of each unit of State and local government; 
        (4) integrate with, leverage, and coordinate, to the maximum extent practicable, the current geospatial activities of other Federal agencies and units of State and local government; and 
        (5) develop a funding strategy to leverage and coordinate budgets and expenditures, and to maintain or establish joint funding and other agreement mechanisms with other Federal agencies and units of State and local government to share in the collection and utilization of geospatial data among all governmental users.

fable.w: The tempting reading is "No", because subsection (a) is purely interagency coordination and a report to congressional committees, both of which stay inside the federal government. But subsection (b)(3)-(5) directs the Administrator, in carrying out the federal flood mapping program, to coordinate with units of State and local government and to set up joint funding and agreement mechanisms with them. That coordination crosses the federal boundary to outside parties, which fits the definition. The call is not certain, since the coordination is operational rather than a formal consultation before a discrete decision.
fable.s: integrate with, leverage, and coordinate funding of, to the maximum extent practicable, the current flood mapping activities of each unit of State and local government

opus.w: Subsection (b)(3)-(5) requires the Administrator (a federal official) to coordinate flood mapping and geospatial activities, funding strategies, and joint funding agreements with units of State and local government, which are outside the federal government. That crosses the federal boundary, so it counts as participation. Subsection (a) alone would be "No" because it covers only coordination among federal agencies and a report to Congress, but that does not cancel out the outside coordination in (b).
opus.s: (3) integrate with, leverage, and coordinate funding of, to the maximum extent practicable, the current flood mapping activities of each unit of State and local government;
opus.b: Step 1, the tempting misreading: the opposite trap applies here. Subsection (a) is entirely internal to the federal government. It covers data-sharing among federal agencies and a budget report to congressional committees, so it would be "No" by itself. If you stopped reading there, you would answer "No." But subsection (b) goes further and directs the Administrator to coordinate with State and local governments, which are outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The primary procedural requirement in this section is the submission of a report to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. While subsection (b) mentions coordinating with state and local governments, this is described as integrating activities and leveraging funding, not as a mandatory consultation or coordination process required before a specific federal decision is made (such as a rulemaking or permit decision). There are no public comment periods, public hearings, advisory boards with non-federal members, or rights to sue mentioned. Thus, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: (2) Report.—Not later than 30 days after the submission of the budget of the United States Government by the President to Congress, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, in coordination with the Federal Emergency Management Agency, the United States Geological Survey, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, the Corps of Engineers, and other Federal agencies, as appropriate, shall submit to the appropriate authorizing and appropriating committees of the Senate and the House of Representatives an interagency budget crosscut and coordination report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that subsection (b)(3) and (b)(4) require the Administrator to "coordinate with... units of State and local government," which are outside the federal government. However, this coordination is regarding the integration of existing activities and funding strategies, not a mandatory consultation or coordination *before* a specific federal decision is made that would constitute "participation" in the sense of influencing a discrete regulatory or policy choice through a formal process like a hearing, comment period, or advisory board. More importantly, the primary procedural requirement in subsection (a) is a report to Congress (inside government). The coordination described in (b) is operational and ongoing, not a pre-decisional participatory mechanism defined by the prompt (e.g., advisory board, public hearing, comment period, right to sue). The prompt emphasizes that "consultation or coordination BETWEEN federal agencies... is not participation." While (b) mentions state/local governments, it frames it as leveraging/integrating activities rather than a formal participatory decision-making process. However, looking closer at the definition: "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government before making a decision." Subsection (b)(3) says "integrate with... current flood mapping activities of each unit of State and local government." This is operational coordination. Subsection (a) is a report to Congress. There is no requirement for a public comment period, public hearing, advisory board with non-federal members, or right to sue. The coordination with states is about data sharing and funding leverage, not a pre-decisional consultation on a specific federal action. Therefore, it is "No".
